markets.question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s entrenched position as paramount leader, reinforced by the abolition of presidential term limits and repeated elite purges that have removed even Politburo and military figures without apparent challenge to his authority, underpins the near-certain trader consensus that he will remain in office through early 2027. With the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027 expected to deliver a fourth term rather than any transition, recent developments including the July 2026 expulsion of Ma Xingrui and ongoing Central Military Commission investigations have been interpreted as extensions of centralized control rather than signs of vulnerability. No designated successor has emerged, succession planning has been deferred at least until 2032, and the absence of visible factional opposition or institutional pressure sustains the high implied probability. Rare events such as a sudden health crisis, unprecedented elite backlash, or abrupt voluntary retirement could still shift outcomes before the congress.
